verdict.rationale: MX's Instant Account Verification returns verified account and routing numbers. It also provides Tokenized Account Numbers (TANs), substitute account numbers meant for secure ACH money movement, so it offers some token-style handoff of verified credentials for payments. The evidence names no third-party processor or platform integration and no processor-token exchange flow. missing for 10: documented integrations with named payment processors (e.g., processor partner list), a token-exchange flow that hands credentials directly to a third-party processor, details on how TANs are consumed by processors, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, linked accounts plug into my payment processor — documented integrations or token exchange that hand verified account credentials to third-party processors and platforms

citations.quote: Tokenized Account Numbers (TANs) are substitute account numbers used for secure ACH money movement.
With Instant Account Verification, you can connect to an end user's financial institution and retrieve account and routing numbers for their demand deposit accounts.
